configKeys.effect: Radius (blocks) in which tamed cats are associated when shift-clicking a bowl.
How many ticks a single fish feeding keeps a cat in the 'fed' (guarding) state (20 ticks = 1 second).
Horizontal radius (blocks, XZ) around the associated bowl in which a fed cat scans for and attacks hostile mobs.
Vertical radius (blocks, Y) around the associated bowl - cats ignore mobs further away vertically.
Radius (blocks) within which a cat without a bowl is automatically associated with a nearby bowl.
How many seconds the (client-side) glow lasts on associated cats when looking at their bowl. Consumed as ticks via getGlowDurationTicks() = value * 20.
Maximum number of cats that can be associated with a single bowl or station. Also the divisor of the feeding station's comparator output.
Maximum XP points a single cat can hold before XP drops normally.
Maximum XP points a feeding station can hold before overflow stays on cats.
XP points consumed per Bottle o' Enchanting produced at the station.
Base fraction of absorbed damage reflected back to the attacker, scaled by the armor's Thorns level (0.0 = none, 1.0 = full).

Read as a raw held-key state (InputConstants.isKeyDown / glfwGetMouseButton, CatGuardianKeybinds#isModifierDown) rather than KeyMapping.isDown(), so it works as a modifier; a mouse-button binding is supported. notes:
PROVENANCE / VERIFICATION
- Re-verified independently against: modules/cat_guardian/** (all 33 files), mixin/cat_guardian/**, modules/debug_overlay/client/{GogglesUtil,DebugOverlayKeybinds,DebugOverlayState}.java, modules/flying_fish/FlyingFishModule.java, vanillaplusadditions.mixins.json, build.gradle (standaloneModules + JEI), META-INF/neoforge.mods.toml, en_us.json, VanillaPlusAdditions.java:167, core/Module.java:73, core/AbstractModuleConfig.java:60+66, core/ModuleManager.java:88-110, README.md, git log/tag. No gradle run (read-only task).

ENABLED BY DEFAULT
- CatGuardianModule overrides neither isEnabledByDefault() nor shouldInitialize(); the Module interface default (core/Module.java:73-75) returns true. Nothing gates initialization on another mod, so requiredMods is empty.

CONFIG
- Exactly the 11 keys above, all via defineInRange in CatGuardianConfig#buildModuleSpecificConfig. The inherited "enabled" (AbstractModuleConfig:60) and "debug_logging" (AbstractModuleConfig:66) keys are framework-wide and deliberately not listed here.

README ACCURACY (checked line by line)
- README.md:25 is WRONG: it claims guardians "dive after underwater mobs with water breathing". The code says the opposite - CatGuardianModule.tickCat() sets the PathType.WATER malus to 0 with the comment "FloatGoal keeps them at the surface - they can never dive anymore" (CatGuardianModule.java:1051-1054), and there is an explicit drowning-escape branch (air < 60 -> drop target, head home, line 1067). Cats cross shallow water only. Do not carry that sentence over.
- README.md:26 is CORRECT and must not be "fixed": the stats popup really is hold-to-peek on the cat keybind (CatGuardianGogglesClientHandler.java:99 popupHeld = CatGuardianKeybinds.isModifierDown()) and the 3D boxes really are on a separate toggle, default Numpad + (line 100, DebugOverlayState.isEnabled()). Both additionally require goggles (line 88). The only nuance worth documenting: that Numpad+ keybind is registered by the debug_overlay module, not by cat_guardian.
- README.md:296 still links docs/cat_guardian.md while the working tree has the file staged as docs/modules/cat_guardian.md - stale link from the in-flight docs reorg.

DEAD / ORPHAN ARTEFACTS
- Lang key "key.vanillaplusadditions.cat_guardian.toggle_overlay" (en_us.json:142) has NO reference anywhere under src/main/java - orphan from when the overlay toggle lived in this module.
- Lang keys "message.vanillaplusadditions.cat_guardian.overlay_on" / ".overlay_off" (en_us.json:157-158) are likewise unreferenced.
- Commented-out dead line in CatGuardianModule#onEntityInteract (line 1354: "// event.setCanceled(false);"); the surrounding comment reads as if guardian cats were the cancelled case, while the control flow actually returns early for NON-guardian cats and cancels only for guardian cats.
- CatGuardianConfig#getAssociationRadius() falls back to 8.0D (CatGuardianConfig.java:64) while the declared spec default is 64.0D and the static CatGuardianModule#getAssociationRadius() falls back to 64.0D (CatGuardianModule.java:265). Only reachable while the spec value is null, but it is an inconsistency.

CROSS-MODULE COUPLINGS (other VPA modules, not optional mods)
- HARD compile-time coupling to flying_fish: CatGuardianModule#isFishItem (line 1002-1012) dereferences FlyingFishModule.RAW_FLYING_FISH.get() / COOKED_FLYING_FISH.get() with no module gate - but only on the fall-through path, i.e. when the held stack is NOT already in #minecraft:fishes. FlyingFishModule attaches its DeferredRegister inside onInitialize() (FlyingFishModule.java:140-141) and ModuleManager.initializeModules() calls initialize() on ENABLED modules only, so with cat_guardian on and flying_fish off those holders stay unbound and .get() is expected to throw the moment a player right-clicks any cat with a non-fish item in hand. Code-structure risk, NOT verified in-game.
- Coupling to debug_overlay: the goggles overlay uses debug_overlay's DebugOverlayState + GogglesUtil. build.gradle:403 declares moduleDeps ['vpa_debug_overlay','vpa_flying_fish'] for the standalone jar, matching both couplings.
- GogglesUtil gates on Create's GogglesItem OR the item tag vanillaplusadditions:arm_goggles. That tag's JSON ships in the arm_target_overlay standalone jar's dataGlobs (build.gradle:388), not in cat_guardian's or debug_overlay's - so in a standalone cat_guardian install without Create AND without arm_target_overlay the tag branch has no data behind it and the overlay is unreachable.
- The #minecraft:fishes additions (flying_fish + cooked_flying_fish) live in data/minecraft/tags/item/fishes.json, which build.gradle:429 ships with the flying_fish module - pulled in via the vpa_flying_fish moduleDep.
- cat_guardian's OWN dataGlobs are only data/minecraft/tags/item/enchantable/armor.json + durability.json (build.gradle:401-402), which make the cat armor enchantable/mendable.

BEHAVIOUR DETAILS WORTH DOCUMENTING
- Association: sneak + right-click with BOTH hands empty on a bowl/station (AbstractCatBowlBlock#associateCatsWithBowl via useWithoutItem) associates every tamed cat of that player within association_radius. Vanilla skips the block interaction entirely when sneaking with an item in hand, so this really is an empty-hand gesture. Bowls/stations cap at max_cats_per_station (message .station_full for the rest, .no_cats when none were found, .associated on success). A bowl-less cat auto-associates within auto_associate_radius during tickCat.
- Non-sneaking empty-hand right-click: bowl ejects its fish back into the player's inventory; station opens its GUI.
- Feeding a bowl/station: only #minecraft:fishes (CatBowlBlock#useItemOn:44, CatFeedingStationBlock#useItemOn:163, CatBowlBlockEntity:17/44, CatFeedingStationBlockEntity#isValidFishType:99-100). The station's useItemOn loops and swallows the whole non-creative stack.
- Hand-feeding a cat: isFishItem additionally accepts the two flying-fish items explicitly (the mod's own fishes.json puts them in the tag anyway). It only takes effect on GUARDIAN cats - a tamed non-guardian cat returns early and keeps vanilla breeding/feeding. Any player may feed any tamed guardian cat; ownership is NOT checked. Effect: fed ticks reset, cat healed to full, CAT_PURREOW, 7 heart particles, one item consumed unless creative, event cancelled.
- Petting: empty main hand + left-click on ANY cat (tame or not, guardian or not) cancels the attack and plays CAT_PURR with 5 heart particles (onAttackCat). Easy to miss and worth documenting.
- Eating from the bowl also grants Regeneration II for 100 ticks (MobEffectInstance(REGENERATION, 100, 1)) and, at a station, triggers a loot transfer.
- Healing at base is a manual heal of 10/50 HP per tickCat pass (every 10 ticks) - STATION_HEAL_PER_PASS, with a long comment explaining that a re-applied Regeneration effect never healed because vanilla checks "duration % 50 == 0" before decrementing.
- Flee logic: below 20% HP the cat drops all targets and runs home (CAT_FLEEING), sits at base until healed, resumes duty only above 40% HP (hysteresis). Ordinary post-combat return (CAT_RETURNING) is interruptible, ends within 4 blocks of the bowl (distSq <= 16) or after 1200 accumulated ticks.
- Combat: armor absorbs 100% of incoming damage and takes ceil(damage) durability; Thorns reflects thorns_reflect_fraction * level; Sharpness on the armor adds 0.5 + 0.5*level outgoing. A guardian cat ONE-SHOTS creepers (damage forced to health + 1000) so the fuse never ignites. Armor tiers: iron 200 dur / +1.0 atk, gold 100 / +2.0, diamond 400 / +3.0, netherite 600 / +4.0 (fire-resistant item); enchantment values 9/25/10/15; repairable with an armadillo scute or the tier's own ingot/gem.
- XP/loot: onMobDamagedByCat sets victim.setLastHurtByPlayer(owner) so vanilla drops XP at all (a cat-only kill otherwise drops none); XP is then redirected into the cat (cat_xp_capacity), handed to the station on deposit (station_xp_capacity) and converted to Bottles o' Enchanting at xp_per_bottle each (CatGuardianModule.java:1250-1252).
- Station item handler: util/StationItemHandler, externalHandler = new StationItemHandler(inventory, lootInventory, true) for every side except DOWN, bottomHandler = ...(.., false) for DOWN (CatFeedingStationBlockEntity.java:79/85, wired in onRegisterCapabilities). Both take anything in (fish -> food chamber, rest -> loot); only the bottom one refuses to hand food back out, so a hopper underneath drains loot + XP bottles but never the cats' fish.
- Station blockstate: FACING (horizontal) + SKIN; comparator output is enabled and returns floorDiv(associatedCats * 15, max_cats_per_station) - i.e. it reports cat occupancy, not fish or loot. CatStationSkin lists 28 values (ORIGINAL + 11 material skins + 16 wool colors), driven by a single deco slot with an item->skin map (wool x16, oak/spruce/dark-oak/cherry/bamboo wood, stone/stone bricks/bricks/deepslate/andesite, copper ingot, gold block, grass block). Skin identifiers are German (gemuetliches_holz, edle_dunkeleiche, ...) - legacy naming, do not rename.
- Cat attribute buffs applied on EntityJoinLevel (server side) for EVERY cat that joins: FOLLOW_RANGE +16 and STEP_HEIGHT +0.9 as permanent modifiers, plus a CatGuardTargetGoal on targetSelector priority 1. These are added regardless of guardian status; only the fence-walking, water maluses and goal suppression are guardian-only (applied in tickCat).
- Client-side-only glow: looking at a bowl re-asserts a local GLOWING shared flag on the looking player's own associated cats for glow_duration_seconds. The old server-side GLOWING effect (visible to everyone) and its RequestCatGlowPacket round-trip were removed; the config key is still named glow_duration_SECONDS but is consumed via getGlowDurationTicks() (value * 20).
- Kitten inheritance: BabyEntitySpawnEvent tames the kitten to one randomly chosen tamed parent's owner (or the only tamed parent) and force-sits it, otherwise FollowOwnerGoal/panic-teleport yanks it across the map.
- Packets: OpenCatInventory + RequestCatStats (to server), SyncCatInventory / SyncCatStats / SyncCatTarget / SyncCatPath (to client) - needed because entity AttachmentTypes do not sync by themselves; isGuardianCat() is server truth only. StartTracking re-sends armor, XP and the current target so the overlay is correct as soon as a player comes into range.
- Recipes are injected in code via AddReloadListenerEvent (project convention: no datapack JSON). Block drops come from an overridden getDrops in AbstractCatBowlBlock (line 48) for the same reason; container contents are dropped in each subclass's onRemove.
- Sable integration is deliberately indirected through SableCatBlocks: putting "new SableCatBowlBlock(...)" directly into the module class makes the verifier load Sable classes while LINKING CatGuardianModule, which crashes without Sable. Do not "simplify" that factory away.

CLIENT-SETUP GATING (observed, worth a look)
- CatGuardianClientSetup, CatGuardianClientEvents and CatGuardianGogglesClientHandler are @EventBusSubscriber classes that FML registers regardless of module state. CatGuardianClientSetup#onRegisterMenuScreens / #onRegisterRenderers call CAT_FEEDING_STATION_MENU.get(), CAT_INVENTORY_MENU.get() and CAT_FEEDING_STATION_BE.get() with no isModuleEnabled() check, and those DeferredHolders are only bound inside onInitialize(). The same pattern exists in axolotl_guardian and item_vault_viewer, so it is house style rather than a cat_guardian-specific slip - but it is the same shape of risk as the flying_fish coupling. Not verified in-game.
oneLiner: Tamed cats you hook up to a fish bowl or feeding station become base guards: they patrol, kill hostile mobs in a configurable radius, haul the loot and XP back to the station, and can wear their own armor.

optionalMods.whatItAdds: Bowl and feeding station are registered as Sable-aware block variants (SableCatBowlBlock / SableCatFeedingStationBlock) so they can ride a contraption; SableBowlAssemblyHandler#afterMove teleports the associated cats into the sublevel on assembly and re-points their stored bowl position at the new block pos. Without Sable the plain blocks are registered and a bowl on a moving ship simply loses its cats (the usual self-healing re-association applies). Declared type="optional", side="CLIENT" in neoforge.mods.toml:98-103.

Create's Engineer's Goggles are one of the two ways to satisfy the goggles requirement for the overlay (cat stats popup, target/radius/path boxes). Without Create only an item in the vanillaplusadditions:arm_goggles tag counts, and that tag's JSON ships with the arm_target_overlay module, not with cat_guardian or debug_overlay. Declared type="optional" in neoforge.mods.toml:82-87.

Adds the cat-armor anvil repair entries (armadillo scute + the tier's own ingot/gem) and the enchantment info to JEI. Without JEI the repairs still work in-game but are undiscoverable - JEI's built-in anvil list is hardcoded vanilla and cannot see a code-only isValidRepairItem. The plugin is loaded only by JEI's annotation scan and is additionally gated on the module being enabled. JEI is compileOnly in build.gradle:110-111 and not declared in neoforge.mods.toml at all.

recipes: cat_armor_iron - shaped "X  "/"XXX"/"S S" with X = iron ingot, S = armadillo scute (category EQUIPMENT)
cat_armor_gold - same pattern with X = gold ingot, S = armadillo scute (EQUIPMENT)
cat_armor_diamond - same pattern with X = diamond, S = armadillo scute (EQUIPMENT)
cat_armor_netherite - same pattern with X = netherite ingot, S = armadillo scute (EQUIPMENT)
cat_bowl - shaped "S S"/"SSS" with S = smooth stone (category MISC)
cat_feeding_station - shaped "GGG"/"GCG"/"SSS" with G = glass pane, C = cauldron, S = smooth stone (category MISC)

All six are injected in code by a PreparableReloadListener added in AddReloadListenerEvent, which merges them into RecipeManager.replaceRecipes(); gated on isModuleEnabled(). No datapack JSON, per the project convention.
shortDescription: Adds cat food bowls and feeding stations. Fed cats actively guard your base against hostile mobs.
